title: Alibaba is raising $10.2bn and spending all of it on AI
excerpt: Alibaba is raising HK$80bn (about $10.2bn) through a share placement in Hong Kong, with all net proceeds earmarked for AI infrastructure and full-stack AI...
content_html:
Alibaba is raising HK$80bn (about $10.2bn) through a share placement in Hong Kong, with all net proceeds earmarked for AI infrastructure and full-stack AI capabilities. The raise comes days after the company reported a 75% drop in quarterly net profit, driven by a 75% jump in capital expenditure to 67.68bn yuan. Cloud and AI revenue rose 45% to 48.44bn yuan, and AI model services now generate over 16bn yuan in annual recurring revenue. The offering is the largest primary follow-on ever by a Hong Kong-listed company and the largest Regulation S equity offering on record, ranking third globally this year behind Alphabet's $85bn raise and Intel. Alibaba is also expanding its European cloud footprint, including new availability zones in Paris, even as the EU's proposed Cloud and AI Development Act could restrict Chinese-headquartered providers from its stricter sovereignty tiers.

    #cloud#venture-capital#ai-infrastructure#alibaba

Questions this post answers

How much is Alibaba raising for AI infrastructure and where is the money coming from?

Alibaba is placing HK$80bn of new shares, about $10.2bn, in Hong Kong, with 100% of net proceeds directed to full-stack AI capabilities including infrastructure. It is the largest primary follow-on offering ever by a Hong Kong-listed company and the largest Regulation S equity offering on record, ranking third globally in 2026 behind Alphabet's $85bn raise and Intel. Follow how major cloud providers are financing AI buildouts by tracking coverage like this on daily.dev.

Why did Alibaba's profit drop while its AI spending increased?

Alibaba's quarterly net profit fell 75% after capital expenditure rose 75% to 67.68bn yuan in the April to June quarter, spent building AI compute capacity. Despite the profit hit, cloud and AI revenue grew 45% to 48.44bn yuan, and AI model services now generate over 16bn yuan in annual recurring revenue, which executives frame as necessary upfront investment for future growth.
